general.nameHint: Shown in the app and when people add this instance.
general.publicUrlHint: The URL people use to reach this instance. Uploaded pictures are linked through it, so set it before people upload.
general.webLabel: Open the app at this address
general.webHint: Turned off, people can still use this instance from the app on another fuwa instance.
general.webNotBuilt: This build of fuwa doesn't include the web app.
origins.hint: Web pages on other sites, such as the fuwa app on another instance, that may use this one from a browser. Signing in with waifu.dev from another site only works for sites listed here by name.
origins.note: One per line, like https://chat.example.com. This page ({page}) always works when served by this instance.
startup.title: Set when the instance starts
startup.hint: Changed only by whoever runs it, through FUWA_* environment variables.
signUps.localHint: A username and password kept on this instance only.
signUps.localOffNeeds: Needs waifu.dev sign-in or single sign-on working first.
signUps.localOffNotice: You sign in here with a password. Once you sign out, you'll need another way in here to get back in.
signUps.linkedHint: People sign in with their waifu.dev account, and get an account here the first time.
signUps.linkedNotice: waifu.dev can only send people back to an https address. Set the public address under General to turn this on.
signUps.issuerHint: The OpenAuth issuer waifu.dev sign-ins go through. Accounts already linked stay tied to the one they came from.
signUps.serversPerAccountHint: How many servers one account may own.
signUps.agentHint: Agents are accounts programs drive, such as bots. Agents already made keep working.
signUps.mcpLabel: Agents can use this instance as an MCP server
signUps.mcpHint: AI apps such as Claude reach it at /mcp with an agent's token and get the same permissions the agent has. Server managers can still pick which agents may use theirs.
signUps.sharedLabel: Servers can share channels with each other
signUps.sharedHint: Admins of two servers here can show one channel in both. Turned off, nobody can start a new one; channels already shared stay until either side ends them.
signUps.effectsLabel: People can put an effect on their profile card
signUps.effectsHint: Petals, stars and the like, drawn by the app from your theme's colors. Turned off, nobody's shows, and everyone's pick comes back when it's on again.
signUps.presenceLabel: People can show what they're doing
signUps.presenceHint: Games and apps people's desktop apps see, shown to people they share a server with, once each person turns it on. Kept in memory only. Turned off, nobody's activity shows; statuses still do.
sso.accountsHint: People sign in through the identity provider below, and get an account here the first time.
sso.setUpFirst: Set up the identity provider first.
sso.notice: Identity providers send people back to this instance's public address, which has to be https. Set it under General.
sso.saveFirst: Save first; the test uses the saved provider.
sso.fillFirst: Fill it in and save first.
limits.defaultHint: A server can get its own caps from its settings. With a cap off, it's unlimited.
limits.defaults: {members} members, {channels} channels, {storage} storage, {files} files, {emoji} emoji, {recordings} recordings
limits.pictureHint: Avatars, banners and server icons. The app crops pictures and saves them small, so only GIFs, which go up as they are, get near a few megabytes.
limits.picturesPerDayHint: How much one account may upload in a day (UTC), so nobody can fill this instance's disk.
limits.attachmentHint: Any file people send with a message: documents, archives, audio, video. Leave it empty for no limit.
limits.attachmentPerDayHint: How much one account may send in files in a day (UTC), apart from pictures.
limits.voiceSecondsHint: In direct messages. Apps stop recording here; voice messages are end-to-end encrypted, so this instance can't check their length itself.
limits.voiceBytesHint: Its encrypted file, which this instance does see. A minute of voice is about 240 KB.
limits.voicePerDayHint: What one account may send in a day (UTC), counted apart from pictures and files.
limits.pollVotesHint: How many times one account may vote, change or take back a vote in polls in a minute. Every vote is a live update to everyone in the channel.
limits.commandsHint: How many times one account may run agents' slash commands or press their buttons in a minute. Each one wakes an agent up.
limits.pinsPerChannelHint: How many messages can be pinned in one channel, and in one thread. Unpinning one makes room.
limits.pinsPerConversationHint: How many messages can be pinned in one direct-message conversation. The instance only keeps which messages are pinned, never what they say.
limits.reactionsPerMessageHint: How many different emoji one message can have as reactions. More people reacting with one already there is always fine.
limits.liveTilesPerChannelHint: How many tiles apps (agents and webhooks) can keep in one channel at once.
limits.liveTileUpdatesHint: How many times a minute one app can set or end tiles in a server.
limits.liveTilePublishHint: The shortest time between two updates of one tile reaching the people who see it. Changes in between are kept, and the latest goes out when the time is up, so a busy scoreboard can't flood everyone.
privacy.label: Send the usage signal daily and error reports hourly
privacy.hint: Helps Waifu Devs see how fuwa is used and fix what breaks. Counts only: no names, messages, ids or addresses. Off, apps on this instance send no reports either.
privacy.counts: How many accounts, servers, channels and messages
privacy.options: Which account and server options are on
privacy.version: fuwa version, OS and a random install id
privacy.errors: Kinds of errors and where, and how long requests took (server and apps)
provider.protocolHint: Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace, Keycloak, Authentik and most others speak one of these.
provider.domainsHint: Only people whose verified email is on one of these get in. Leave it empty to let in anyone the provider signs in.
provider.issuerHint: Its /.well-known/openid-configuration says where everything else is.
provider.clientHint: From the app you register for fuwa at the provider, as a confidential web app.
provider.scopes: More scopes, if your provider needs them (openid email profile are always asked for)
provider.notMetadata: That doesn't look like identity provider metadata.
provider.noRedirect: Filled in what it had; it lists no HTTP-Redirect sign-in URL.
provider.metadataHint: Paste the XML your provider offers to fill in the rest.
provider.entityHint: The provider's entity ID (the Issuer its responses carry) and where people sign in (HTTP-Redirect).
provider.certificatesHint: Responses must be signed by one of these, with RSA or ECDSA over SHA-256 or stronger. Up to four, PEM.
provider.tellOidc: Allow this redirect URI on the app you registered.
provider.tellSaml: Add fuwa as a service provider with these. Sign the response or the assertion; don't encrypt it.
provider.testHint: Signs in through the provider as yourself and shows who it said you are.
accounts.turnOffHint: They're signed out on every device and can't sign in until an admin turns the account back on. Their messages and servers stay.
accounts.turnOffAdmin: They stop being an instance admin too.
accounts.newPasswordHint: Send it to them privately. It's shown only this once; they can change it in their account settings after signing in.
accounts.twoStepOff: Two-step sign-in is off for them now. They can set it up again after signing in.
accounts.resetHint: They get a new random password and are signed out everywhere. Their old password stops working.
accounts.alsoTwoStepHint: For someone who lost their authenticator app and their backup codes.
accounts.hiddenShow: Hidden by streamer mode. Show it anyway
announcement.previewHint: What everyone on this instance sees at the top of the app.
announcement.messageHint: Bold, italics, code and links work. Keep it to a line or two.
announcement.placeholder: We're moving to a bigger server tonight at 10 PM. Expect a few minutes offline.
announcement.infoHint: News and small notes. People can close it.
announcement.warningHint: Maintenance or a change coming soon.
announcement.criticalHint: Something is wrong now. Nobody can close it.
announcement.comesDownHint: It disappears from every client by itself at the end.
announcement.comesDownAt: Comes down {time}, counted from when you put it up.
calls.label: Let people talk in voice channels and call in direct messages
calls.hint: Turning it off hangs up every call within a few seconds.
calls.notRunning: not running, so calls can't connect. Whoever runs this instance sets it up (FUWA_MEDIA_PORT, or FUWA_MEDIA_URL for a split instance).
calls.setAtStart: Set when the instance starts. Calls in direct messages are end-to-end encrypted: it only ever forwards sound it can't read.
calls.recordLabel: Let people with Record keep voice channels' recordings on this instance
calls.recordHint: One Ogg Opus track per person, kept with the server's files (sealed when the instance encrypts its files). Nobody has Record until a server's admins grant it. Turning this off stops recordings going on now; the ones kept stay. How much each server may keep is a cap under Limits.
calls.videoLabel: Let servers keep cameras and shared screens in their recordings too
calls.videoHint: Each server's admins choose it under Recordings in their settings. A WebM file per camera and screen, next to the sound: an hour of a camera takes several times the room of the sound, against the same caps under Limits. Turning this off turns it off in every server and ends the recordings filming now.
calls.keepHint: Finished recordings older than this delete themselves, files and copies included. Off keeps them until someone deletes them.
calls.cameraHeightHint: The tallest camera picture anyone sends in this instance's calls. Without a ceiling, apps send the best the camera gives, up to 1080p. Servers can set a lower one for their voice channels.
calls.cameraFpsHint: The most camera frames a second anyone sends. Without a ceiling, apps send up to 60.
calls.iceHint: For people behind strict firewalls: a TURN server relays their sound when nothing else gets through. One per line, as stun:, turn: or turns: addresses.
calls.turnHint: The shared secret your TURN server (such as coturn with use-auth-secret) checks. Apps get a new password from it for each call, good for an hour, that names no account.
release.runs: This instance runs {current}. Nothing updates by itself: pull the new image or binary when it suits you.
release.runsCameOut: This instance runs {current}; {version} came out {when}. Nothing updates by itself: pull the new image or binary when it suits you.
federation.intro: With this on, this instance talks to other fuwa instances so servers can share channels across them. Only the instances talk: apps here never connect to another instance, and no one's address is passed on. Every call is signed with this instance's key and checked against the key pinned for the other one. With shared channels on too, a server here can share a channel with a server on another instance, and messages pass between the two through the instances. Below you can check that two instances reach each other.
federation.label: Share channels with other instances
federation.hint: Off, this instance answers other instances with nothing but “off”. Turning it off later stops every call between instances.
federation.knownAs: Other instances know this one as {origin}.
federation.compare: Before sharing with another instance, compare fingerprints with its admins somewhere you trust: theirs shows here once the two have met.
federation.rotateBody: A new key replaces this one, and the old key vouches for it, so instances that know this one move to the new key by themselves. Signed calls on their way when it changes are turned away once. Rotating doesn't help if the key was stolen: then other instances' admins check this one again and compare the new fingerprint with you somewhere you trust.
federation.noPeers: None yet. An instance shows here once an admin here checks it.
federation.blockedHint: Host names, one a line. This instance never calls them and turns their calls away.
federation.sendsHint: How many messages all the people of one server on another instance may send together to channels shared from here. That instance says who its people are, so a server there counts as one sender.
federation.peopleHint: How many people one server on another instance may bring to a server's shared channels. Past it, no one new from that server can join in; those already there still can.
federation.filesHint: How much one server on another instance may send in files to channels shared from here in a day (UTC). The files are kept here, under the home server's room for files.
federation.fetchesHint: How many files this instance fetches from other instances at the same time, for shared channels; each instance gets at most half, and the rest wait their turn. Leave it empty for no limit.
federation.needsCheck: Its key changed in a way its old key didn't vouch for, so nothing goes either way. Compare its new fingerprint with its admins somewhere you trust, then check it above.

federation.movedMany.one: Moved to this key {when} from {fingerprint} ({count} move)
federation.movedMany.other: Moved to this key {when} from {fingerprint} ({count} moves)

federation.checkHint: Fetches its key and pins it here, then sends it a signed greeting there and back. The other instance only checks the greeting: it pins this one's key when its own admins check this instance.
federation.reached: Reached {origin} and back in {ms} ms. Its key: {fingerprint}.
federation.knownThere: It knows this instance too, so signed calls go both ways.
federation.notKnownThere: It doesn't know this instance yet: its admins check this one from their side to pin its key.
gifs.providerHint: Where the GIF button's search, trending and moods come from. This instance asks the provider for everyone and hands back every picture itself, so the provider never sees anyone's address, account or what they send, and apps load nothing from it. A GIF someone sends is stored here, without its metadata, so it stays after the provider drops it.
gifs.offHint: No GIF button. GIFs already sent still show.
gifs.giphyHint: Recommended: the biggest library. Free key at developers.giphy.com.
gifs.klipyHint: A Tenor-style library. Free key from klipy.com.
gifs.keyHint: Kept on this instance (encrypted with its files when it encrypts them) and never sent back to any app, this page included. {name}'s terms ask for "Powered by {name}" by results; the picker shows it.
gifs.keyMissing: GIFs stay off until a key is saved.
gifs.ratingHint: The most a result may be rated. The provider decides ratings; AutoMod's picture checks still look at what's sent.
gifs.capsHint: Off means no cap. Searches kept from the last ten minutes don't count toward the daily calls.
gifs.calls: Calls to the provider a day
gifs.bigger: Bigger GIFs are stored at the provider's smaller size, or refused when even that is over {size}.
moderation.jevBlurb: A decision model that answers yes-or-no questions about a text with a calibrated probability. Text only, run in the US.
moderation.jevKeyHelp: An API key from your TypeSafe account. Billed per word read, by TypeSafe.
moderation.clefBlurb: Cloudflare's open decision models on Workers AI, answering the same questions as Jev. Runs on Cloudflare's network.
moderation.clefKeyHelp: An API token with Workers AI Read, either an account token (Manage Account, Account API Tokens) or a user token (My Profile, API Tokens), and your account id from the dashboard's sidebar. Billed by Cloudflare.
moderation.intro: Turn a service on here and every server on this instance can pick it for AutoMod's smart filter, with one switch. Only this instance talks to it, and only about messages in servers that turned the filter on: their text, never who wrote them, where, or the server's name. If it's slow or down, messages go through and the servers' own rules still apply.
moderation.checksHint: How many messages each server's smart filter may send to its provider in a day (UTC), so one busy server can't run up your bill. Once a server uses them, its messages go through the smart filter unchecked until midnight UTC, like when the provider is down: blocking every message instead would stop a busy server talking. Its own rules still apply, and its Usage page shows how many are left.

moderation.max.one: That's {count}, the most an instance keeps.
moderation.max.other: That's {count}, the most an instance keeps.

moderation.addOwnHint: A classifier you run, or any https address that answers the same questions as Jev and Clef. What it gets and answers is in docs/automod.md.
moderation.customBlurb: Yours, at an https address you pick. It gets the same questions as Jev and Clef.
moderation.customKeyHelp: If it needs one. It goes as Authorization: Bearer, or in the header you name.
moderation.goesTo: Turned on, messages that servers choose to check go from this instance to {host}, which sees their text. Nothing else goes: no names, ids, servers or addresses.
moderation.namePlaceholder: What servers see, like Our classifier
moderation.httpsOnly: fuwa only talks to https addresses, like https://moderation.example.com/v1/check.
moderation.retypeKey: New address: type the key again
moderation.savedEnds: Saved, ends in {hint}. Type to replace it.
moderation.kept: Kept on the instance, sealed with its files when it encrypts them, and never shown again.
moderation.addName: Add a name to test it and turn it on.
moderation.addAddress: Add an https address to test it and turn it on.
moderation.addKey: Add the key to test it and turn it on.
moderation.addNameAddress: Add a name and an https address to test it and turn it on.
moderation.addNameKey: Add a name and the key to test it and turn it on.
moderation.addAddressKey: Add an https address and the key to test it and turn it on.
moderation.addAll: Add a name and an https address and the key to test it and turn it on.
moderation.addTokenAccount: Add the token and account id to test it and turn it on.
servers.none: Nobody has made a server here yet.
servers.endHomeBody: It goes away from {server}. Messages stay with this server, and both servers' admins see it in the audit log.
servers.endGuestBody: It goes away from this server. Messages stay with {server}, and both servers' admins see it in the audit log.
servers.moveWhat: Its messages, channels, roles, recordings, icon, emoji and webhook pictures go to {to}, and nothing of them is kept in {from}.
servers.moveWait: Changes wait a moment while it travels. People in its calls are dropped and can rejoin.
servers.deleteHint: Everyone loses its channels and messages. Save its file first if you might want it back.
nav.signInProvidersAbout: Let people sign in here with their Google, X or Twitch account.
providers.accountsHint: Whether someone new who signs in with one of these gets an account here. People can link them to an account they already have either way, unless they're off.
providers.closedHint: Only accounts that linked one already
providers.offHint: Nobody signs in or links with them
providers.allOff: Everything here is off until New accounts is set to Open or Linked only.
providers.providerHint: This instance talks to {name} itself. Apps never load anything from {name}, and {name} sees only who signs in.
providers.makeApp: Make an app for this instance at {name}, give it the address below, then paste its client ID and secret here:
providers.xScopes: X asks which scopes the app needs: turn on users.read and tweet.read. X won't share who signed in without tweet.read; this instance never reads posts.
providers.needsAddress: Save this instance's public address first; the provider sends people back to it.
providers.missing: It needs both a client ID and a secret before it can be saved.
providers.twitchState: Twitch doesn't offer PKCE, so only this instance's one-time state ties Twitch's answer to the sign-in that asked for it. Keep the client secret private.
nav.profileItemsAbout: Effects and avatar decorations everyone on this instance can wear.
signUps.decorationsLabel: People can wear a decoration around their avatar
signUps.decorationsHint: Pictures from the instance's and servers' profile items. Turned off, nobody's shows, and everyone's pick comes back when it's on again.
